name: form-actions
title: Form actions
description: The button row that ends a form: primary last, Cancel beside it, a destructive action kept apart, a pending state, a hint and an optional sticky bar.
docs: primary is the main button (label, onClick, type, disabled) and is last in the DOM, so Tab finishes on it; secondary is the quiet one beside it (usually Cancel) and never submits; start is a slot at the far start for an action of another kind, such as Delete project. pending switches every button off together, shows a spinner on the primary without changing its label, sets aria-busy on the row and tells a screen reader once (labels.pending). The browser drops the focus of a button that is switched off, so the row gives it back to the primary when the wait ends. hint is a polite live region for a line such as Unsaved changes. align places the buttons at the end (default) or the start, sticky pins the row to the bottom of its scroll container with a hairline above and safe-area padding, and under 480px of the row's own width the buttons stack at full width with the primary on top (a visual order: Tab still goes Cancel, then the primary). From 480px up the row wraps rather than squeezes: the hint keeps the width of its words, and what does not fit goes to a line of its own. shortcut makes Command or Control plus Enter press the primary from anywhere in the form, also in a textarea: on (default), hint (also shows the keys on the button) or off. The press is a click on the primary, so onClick, native validation and the form's onSubmit all run as for a mouse press.
